3090022.findings: Two studio pottery vases in a single photo with no base shown, so no signature or maker's mark can be read and the Rynne Tanton attribution rests on the catalogue alone. Left vase: squat globular form with a flared turquoise collar and a mottled blue crystalline-type glaze over incised chevron or feather texture. Right vase: ovoid form with a flared glossy red-brown collar and a white crackle glaze over exposed brown stoneware in a cracked-earth pattern. Rynne Tanton (b. 1944, Launceston area, Tasmania) is a recognised Australian studio potter known for crackle and crystalline glazes, with a 1977 covered jar in the NGV collection; a Sydney dealer (Cache Antiques) has asked A$280 for a single signed Tanton crackle/crystalline vase (17 cm). The glaze styles here are consistent with his work, but this is unverified from the photo. Size not stated.

3090022.reason: Two crackle and crystalline-glaze studio vases attributed to Rynne Tanton, a collected Launceston potter whose signed pieces retail around A$280 each; attribution unverified (no base shown).
3090022.marks_read: none visible (no base photo); signature not shown

3090024.findings: The gilt-framed piece is not a generic French print: it is a steel engraving titled Approach to Richmond from North Bank of Yarra Yarra, lettered S.T. Gill del. at lower left (read), with an engraver's credit at lower right that is too blurred to read (the NGV records this plate as engraved by J. Tingle), and the imprint Published by Sands & Kenny, Melbourne & Sydney, 1856 (the NGV records the same inscription; the series is Victoria Illustrated, published 1857). Photos cannot show whether it is an original or a later reprint (Sands & McDougall reissued Gill plates c.1890); comparable single plates retail around $110-130 unframed. Frame looks like a period gilt gesso frame with a beaded inner slip and a cream and gilt mount. The lot also has a loose, unframed sheet carrying a hand-coloured vignette: two men in straw hats planting a vegetable bed beside a verandah cottage, with a long shed and a river with rowing boats behind. It is unsigned in the photos and is in a colonial manner that could be Gill (could be a coloured print, or possibly a watercolour), maker unconfirmed. The title's French print is not identifiable, so the title may be mixing up the two pieces.

3090024.reason: Documented S.T. Gill / Tingle steel engraving (Victoria Illustrated, Sands & Kenny) in a period gilt frame plus a loose Gill-style coloured vignette that is worth far more if it proves to be an original; likely $150-300 with upside.
